page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.4-16 is a virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8358 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core, delivering 8 vCPUs to the guest environment. System memory is provisioned at 16.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance does not incorporate bundled local storage, meaning operating system disks and persistent data volumes must be configured via network-attached block storage. The platform includes no graphical processing units or hardware accelerators. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

With a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, the resource distribution favors processing capacity over massive in-memory footprints. This profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for organizations that require dedicated multi-threaded compute performance without paying for surplus memory allocations. VM.Standard3.Flex.4-16 is designed for compute-bound tasks, continuous integration workers, web application serving, batch processing pipelines, and distributed microservices.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.4-16 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8358 processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system delivers 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, accompanied by 16.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. This configuration contains no bundled local storage, requiring external block storage for data persistence, and includes no GPU accelerators. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned for direct network connectivity. The instance provides dedicated processing capability without the overhead of oversized memory arrays, yielding favorable resource efficiency for compute-focused architectures. VM.Standard3.Flex.4-16 is suited for parallel processing workloads, web application serving, continuous integration tasks, ETL workers, and distributed microservices that operate effectively within moderate memory footprints.
